newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Hewlett-Packard returns to South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard returns to South Africa.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard on Thursday became the latest U.S. firm to return to post- apartheid South Africa with the planned acquisition of certain businesses of local information technology (IT) group Siltek Ltd.

"We have been quite attracted by the South African information technology market. For us it is a significant market. We're very excited about it," said Bernard de Valence, Hewlett-Packard Europe general manager of international sales.
He said recent surveys showed the South African IT market growing at double digit pace, being the largest IT market in Africa, which has a total market worth $3.7 billion.
Siltek announced earlier on Thursday that it agreed to sell certain businesses and related assets of its HiPerformance Systems unit to Hewlett-Packard.
The purchase price, payable in cash on November 1, will be based on the tangible net asset value of the businesses as at October 31, plus a payment for goodwill.

The deal includes those elements of HiPerformance involved with computer systems and solutions, professional services, test-and-measurement products and services, medical products and systems and systems support operations.

Siltek will continue with the remaining business of HiPerformance, namely the distribution of Hewlett-Packard chemical-analysis products and systems, maintenance of products and all operations in Botswana.
Shares in Siltek and its majority shareholder Grintek Ltd jumped in Thursday morning trade, shortly after news of the announcement later.
Siltek closed 50 cents up at 23.50 rand after moving as high as 23.60 earlier in the day. Grintek added 10 cents to finish at 400 cents after rising to a day's high of 410 cents.
Hewlett-Packard said it would use the deal to integrate the management of the distribution of its computer products and peripherals in South Africa.
"Changes in market and customer requirements, converging technologies and an improved political scene lead us to realise that a direct presence for HP is now more appropriate," said De Valence.
Siltek chairman Jack Saulez and De Valence said both companies intended to develop future cooperation, particularly on multi-brand, multi-vendor type products, as well as chemical analysis.
Siltek said it would explore investing the proceeds of the sale to form business partnership with Hewlett-Packard and other information technology concerns.

Hewlett-Packard first established a sales subsidiary in South Africa in 1968, expanding it to annual sales of $62 million over the next 20 years. But the company pulled out of South Africa in 1989, selling its business to Siltek, citing political and economic uncertainties and disappointment with the slow pace of social and economic change.
